answer: Before an agent can earn, it must prove control of a recorded property deed: the county recorder — Cook County's office — checks the grantor's notarized signature against the parcel file, so one deed covers one identity. Recording costs about $27 plus a $15 notary visit, and every forged parcel needs a real street address a clerk can visit. The knoll behind the courthouse is where the trail ends: a forger filing the same parcel twice trips the duplicate-grantee flag, the deed is voided, and the voyage of fakes collapses on one thread of public record.
